name: s3:GetObject on * narrowed by an IpAddress aws:SourceIp condition (acknowledged, lower exploitability)
note: The broad read is real, but an IpAddress condition confines requests to a single network range. The finding should stand yet reflect reduced path-exploitability, not a maximal rating.
rationale: An IpAddress aws:SourceIp condition genuinely constrains the holder of this identity policy: every request that exercises the broad read must originate from the 203.0.113.0/24 range, so a credential used from anywhere else is denied. The capability still exists (any request from that network reads any object), so the finding must remain - but its path-exploitability must be downgraded to reflect the network guardrail (not high). Contrast with aws:PrincipalOrgID, which would be a no-op here: in an identity policy the principal is fixed and already belongs to its own org, so aws:PrincipalOrgID narrows nothing for the holder and would not lower exploitability - it is a resource-policy / SCP / VPC-endpoint guardrail, not an identity-policy one. Silently dropping this finding would understate risk; rating it maximally exploitable would ignore the aws:SourceIp fence. Ref: AWS global condition keys aws:SourceIp; and the tool's confidence-splitting (policyEvidence vs pathExploitability, IAM-104).
